rows.title: Bracket validation service
rows.source: function solve(s){const st=[],pairs={")":"(","]":"[","}":"{"};for(const c of s){if("([{ ".trim().includes(c))st.push(c);else if(st.pop()!==pairs[c])return false;}return true;}

Context marker: INTERVIEW-111-feda68c18ab58993.

The correctness bug is the final `return true;` in `src/core.mjs`: it accepts input without checking that all opening brackets were closed.

A smallest valid counterexample is `"("`. The loop pushes `"("` onto `st`, then ends with that opening bracket still present. Actual: `solve("(")` returns `true`; required: `false`, because the brackets are unbalanced. Empty input correctly returns `true`, so no shorter counterexample exists.

automatic.answer: This is a small, dependency-free JavaScript ES-module project for validating balanced and correctly nested parentheses, square brackets, and braces. Its core is the synchronous `solve(s)` function in `src/core.mjs`, which uses a stack; `src/service.mjs` exposes a thin `execute(...args)` wrapper, and Node’s built-in test runner provides one smoke test. One important bug is that `solve` returns true without checking whether the stack is empty, so unmatched opening brackets incorrectly pass validation.

This is a small, dependency-free JavaScript ES-module service that validates balanced, correctly nested brackets: (), [], and {}. Its current context marker is INTERVIEW-111-feda68c18ab58993-PATCH-5cd51362749c.

The core is the synchronous `solve(s)` in `src/core.mjs`: it pushes opening brackets onto a stack, checks closing brackets against the latest opening, and requires an empty stack at the end; empty input is valid. `src/service.mjs` provides a thin `execute(...args)` wrapper, while `npm test` runs one smoke test through Node’s built-in test runner.
